problem: Prior CVDN/NDH navigators treat dialog history as a static VLN-style instruction, do not learn visio-linguistic concept association in new environments, and do not learn when to ask questions (RMM uses a hard-coded 'ask every 4th step' heuristic).
motivation: Interactive robots must decide when to ask for help and ground dialog in what they see. Cross-modal pre-training with object tags (OSCAR) offers a way to align visual semantics with text, but web images differ from navigation views, so navigation-specific pre-training and a separate question-asking head are proposed.
key_idea: Initialize from OSCAR, add navigation-specific semantics-aligned pre-training (MLM, masked object-tag prediction, directional grounding), fine-tune with a panoramic viewpoint-selection LSTM decoder, and train a separate frozen-stack binary head to decide when to ask vs navigate.
insight: Each pre-training objective adds value cumulatively: masked object tag prediction gives large gains over the MLM-only stage, and directional grounding gives the best Val Seen results and improves GP and nDTW (Table 1). Viewpoint selection greatly outperforms turn-based actions (Val Unseen SR 32.52 vs 14.77). Multi-task fine-tuning with long RxR trajectories raises GP but lowers SPL, SR and nDTW, so there is a GP/SPL trade-off, and NDH+R2R+R4R gives the best SPL.
method: Encoder: OSCAR-style Transformer over Word-Tag-Image input; 36-view panorama Faster R-CNN region features plus a 128-d heading/elevation direction embedding; extra delimiter tokens for target hint, navigator questions and guide answers.
Two-stage pre-training: OSCAR web weights, then navigation pre-training on NDH and R2R trajectories.

Navigation pre-training objectives: Masked Language Modeling, Masked Object Tag Prediction (predicting over Faster R-CNN classes), and Directional Grounding (CLS state predicts the direction of the next node).
Action decoder: attention-based LSTM taking the previous action and panoramic ResNet features, attending over the encoder output; supports viewpoint selection or turn-based actions.

Question-asking head: a randomly initialized two-layer feed-forward head with binary cross-entropy, trained by imitation on top of the frozen navigator so navigation is unaffected; supervision comes from the ask/navigate time-steps in elongated CVDN instances.
Multi-task fine-tuning with RxR, or R2R+R4R, on top of NDH.
General game-play mode: removes the every-4th-step asking heuristic, since the navigator decides when to ask.

setting.backbone: OSCAR-initialized Transformer encoder + LSTM action decoder (trained/fine-tuned)
setting.training_data: OSCAR web image-text pre-training weights (Conceptual Captions, COCO, Flickr30K, GQA); navigation pre-training on NDH+R2R; fine-tuning on NDH (~4k instances, human navigator supervision), optionally multi-task with RxR (English) or R2R+R4R
setting.observation: 36-view panoramic RGB with Faster R-CNN region features, object tags, ResNet panoramic features, plus dialog history text
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoint selection (also turn-based low-level actions as an ablation)
setting.privileged: none for the navigator (uses navigation graph connectivity; guide answers are pre-collected human dialog)

numbers_note: Question-asking head (RxR checkpoint): accuracy 68.05/67.87 and balanced accuracy 63.33/61.09 (Val Seen/Val Unseen).
results: VISITRON obtains a hidden-test GP of 3.11 (competitive, below MT-RCM+EnvAg's 3.91). Its NDH+R2R+R4R variant reaches state-of-the-art SPL of 25 (vs PREVALENT's 24) at GP 2.40. The question-asking head gets 67.87% accuracy and 61.09% balanced accuracy on Val Unseen.
limitations: Trade-off between GP and SPL: long RxR trajectories raise GP but hurt SPL, SR and nDTW.
Does not evaluate the proposed general game-play mode with a guide, and does not train a question generator.
Needs a navigation graph and English-only data, and is evaluated only in a static simulator with no speech errors.
